process_area.title: Surety Facility Strategy, Provider Management & Program Governance

value_stream.name: Performance Bond, Surety & Bank Guarantee Management

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, Treasury (links to VS-18), Finance (links to VS-17), B2G Sales (links to VS-46), B2B/Project Sales (links to VS-11), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Risk (links to VS-21.2), Cross-Entity Shared Services (links to VS-72), Insurance (links to VS-26)
fields.Trigger: Annual finance/treasury planning (links to VS-33.1/VS-18); business/B2G strategy

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews terms, PMO/Operations delivers the contract" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the authority matrix" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: Surety Program Manager authority; operational: instrument-mix strategy
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Bonds arranged ad-hoc by Sales with no program view; mitigated by Surety Program Manager authority
- **Instrument-mix-suboptimality risk**: Defaulting to cash retention or bank guarantee when surety bond is cheaper/frees credit; mitigated by instrument-mix strategy
System Touchpoints: - Treasury (links to VS-18); finance (links to VS-17); B2G/B2B sales (links to VS-46/VS-11); legal (links to VS-100.3); risk (links to VS-21.2); governance (links to VS-36); cross-entity (links to VS-72)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/Treasury define the surety program strategy and governance: scope (bid/performance/payment/warranty bonds, bank guarantees, LC-for-guarantee, cash retention/escrow), the instrument-mix strategy (surety bond vs. bank guarantee vs. cash vs. LC by contract type), the regulatory map (RA 9184 government procurement, Insurance Code for surety, BSP for bank guarantees), the operating model, and the KPIs (facility utilization, premium cost, encumbrance, claim rate, release cycle-time)

Surety Program Manager establish the governance: Surety Program Manager role/authority, the cross-functional responsibilities (Sales initiates the need, Treasury/Finance arranges the instrument, Legal reviews terms, PMO/Operations delivers the contract), the surety policy, and the integration to treasury (VS-18), B2G (VS-46), B2B (VS-11), and risk (VS-21.2)

CFO/CEO ratify the surety strategy and policy, approve the authority matrix (W3647) and facility envelope (W3642), allocate the program budget (links to VS-17.4), and report surety posture and exposure to the executive risk committee (links to VS-21.2/VS-36) and board (links to VS-36); communicate the mandate

fields.Participants: Treasury (links to VS-18), Surety Program Manager, Finance (links to VS-17), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Surety Companies/Banks, Risk (links to VS-21.2), IC/BSP regulators

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Treasury/Surety Program Manager arrange the surety facility/line" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Treasury/Surety Program Manager manage the facility lifecycle" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-577 (ensure controlled execution — Surety Facility Strategy, Provider Management & Program Governance (PA-116.1).)
- operational: pipeline-based sizing; operational: risk assessment and collateral strategy (W3644)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Insufficient-capacity risk**: Facility too small to support bids, causing bid rejection or cash tie-up; mitigated by pipeline-based sizing
- **Indemnity-exposure risk**: GAI exposes BuildRight to full bond amount on any claim; mitigated by risk assessment and collateral strategy (W3644)
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/banking (links to VS-18.2); finance (links to VS-17); legal (links to VS-100.3); governance/board (links to VS-36); cash positioning (links to VS-18.1); encumbrance register (links to W3654)

steps.activity: Treasury/Surety Program Manager arrange the surety facility/line: aggregate surety capacity across surety companies (IC-regulated) and bank-guarantee lines (BSP-regulated, links to VS-18.2), sized to BuildRight's projected B2G/B2B pipeline, multi-year, and renewable; negotiate terms, limit, sub-limits by bond type/contract size, and the counter-indemnity/collateral requirements

Treasury/Legal negotiate the General Agreement of Indemnity (GAI) / counter-indemnity with surety providers (BuildRight indemnifies the surety for any bond paid), and the bank-guarantee facility agreement (including cash-margin/collateral terms); manage the corporate authorization, board resolution (links to VS-36), and entity-level signatories for the 5 entities

Treasury/Surety Program Manager manage the facility lifecycle: utilization tracking (W3654), renewal/extension, limit optimization (W3645), and provider diversification; report facility health, utilization, and capacity to governance (W3661) and treasury/cash planning (links to VS-18.1)

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, Treasury (links to VS-18), Procurement (links to VS-34), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Finance (links to VS-17), Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03), Risk (links to VS-21.2)

workflows.name: Surety Provider & Bank Guarantee Relationship Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Surety Program Manager/Treasury/Procurement qualify and select surety providers and" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "Surety Program Manager/Treasury manage the provider relationship and contracts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor provider performance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-577 (ensure controlled execution — Surety Facility Strategy, Provider Management & Program Governance (PA-116.1).)
- operational: diversification; operational: financial-strength due diligence
Pain Points / Risks: - **Provider-concentration risk**: Over-reliance on one surety/bank; mitigated by diversification
- **Provider-weakness risk**: Surety company financial distress fails to pay a bond when needed; mitigated by financial-strength due diligence
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-34/VS-03); treasury/banks (links to VS-18.2); legal (links to VS-100.3); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67); analytics (links to W3662)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/Treasury/Procurement qualify and select surety providers and guarantee banks: IC-licensed surety companies with the relevant bond classes and capacity, and BuildRight's relationship banks (BDO/BPI/Metrobank/Chinabank per profile §10.4) for guarantees; due diligence on financial strength, claim handling, turnaround, and coverage

Surety Program Manager/Treasury manage the provider relationship and contracts: master agreements, pricing (W3645), turnaround SLAs, claim protocol (W3658), and the approved-provider list; diversify providers to avoid concentration and ensure competition

Surety Program Manager monitor provider performance: turnaround, pricing, claim handling, capacity utilization, and financial health; re-qualify periodically, manage the approved list, and feed to the scorecard (links to VS-67) and governance (W3662); manage provider exit/replacement

fields.Participants: Treasury (links to VS-18), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Surety Program Manager, Finance (links to VS-17), Risk (links to VS-21.2), Corporate Secretary (links to VS-36)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Treasury/Legal maintain the counter-indemnity framework" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Treasury/Finance manage collateral and security" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report indemnity/collateral exposure to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-577 (ensure controlled execution — Surety Facility Strategy, Provider Management & Program Governance (PA-116.1).)
- operational: collateral optimization (W3645); operational: contract-risk assessment and project delivery
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-collateralization risk**: Excess collateral ties up cash unnecessarily; mitigated by collateral optimization (W3645)
- **Indemnity-call-exposure risk**: GAI exposes BuildRight to full payment on a claim; mitigated by contract-risk assessment and project delivery
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/cash (links to VS-18.1); finance/accounting (links to VS-17); legal (links to VS-100.3); corporate secretary (links to VS-36); risk (links to VS-21.2); encumbrance register (links to W3654)

steps.activity: Treasury/Legal maintain the counter-indemnity framework: the GAI / corporate indemnity to sureties, the entity-level indemnity for the 5 entities, the collateral/security pledged (cash margin, time deposits, letters of credit, assets), and the corporate authorizations/board resolutions (links to VS-36); manage the legal documentation

Treasury/Finance manage collateral and security: cash margin/collateral held by the bank/surety (encumbering cash links to VS-18.1), time-deposit/asset pledges, and the accounting treatment (restricted cash, contingent liability disclosure links to VS-17); track collateral per bond/facility

Treasury/Legal manage collateral release on bond release (links to W3657), substitution of collateral, and dispute over collateral (links to VS-100); report indemnity/collateral exposure to governance (W3661) and risk (links to VS-21.2)

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, Treasury (links to VS-18), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Procurement (links to VS-34), Surety Companies/Banks, BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Facility renewal (W3642); pricing review; cost-reduction cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "capture and benchmark surety pricing" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "discount and diversify providers for competition" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track cost-per-bond and facility utilization, and feed optimization to facility…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-577 (ensure controlled execution — Surety Facility Strategy, Provider Management & Program Governance (PA-116.1).)
- operational: benchmarking and competition; operational: instrument-mix analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-payment risk**: Paying above-market surety premiums; mitigated by benchmarking and competition
- **Suboptimal-mix risk**: Using bank guarantee/cash when surety bond is cheaper/frees capacity; mitigated by instrument-mix analysis
System Touchpoints: - Treasury (links to VS-18); finance (links to VS-17.4); procurement (links to VS-34); BI (links to VS-28.1); facility strategy (links to W3642); analytics (links to W3661)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/Treasury capture and benchmark surety pricing: premium rates by bond type/contract value/risk/term, bank-guarantee fees, LC fees, cash-retention opportunity cost, and collateral cost; benchmark across providers and market

Surety Program Manager/Treasury optimize the instrument mix and providers: surety bond (off-balance-sheet, frees credit) vs. bank guarantee (encumbers credit) vs. cash retention (ties cash) vs. LC, based on cost, capacity, and customer acceptance; consolidate volume for discount and diversify providers for competition

Surety Program Manager/Finance publish surety cost analytics and optimization savings to executives (links to VS-33.2) and governance (W3661), track cost-per-bond and facility utilization, and feed optimization to facility strategy (W3642) and provider management (W3643)

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, Treasury (links to VS-18), B2G/B2B Sales (links to VS-46/VS-11), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Risk (links to VS-21.2), PMO (links to VS-112)
fields.Trigger: Pipeline/bid cycle; capacity review; treasury/cash planning (links to VS-18.1)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "forecast the surety demand from the B2G/B2B pipeline" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-flag of "flag capacity constraints and arrange additional facility if needed" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report capacity/encumbrance and risk to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: demand forecasting and pre-arranged facility; operational: encumbrance planning and instrument optimization
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-shortfall risk**: Insufficient facility to support a winning bid; mitigated by demand forecasting and pre-arranged facility
- **Over-encumbrance risk**: Facilities over-encumbered, constraining operations; mitigated by encumbrance planning and instrument optimization
System Touchpoints: - Sales pipeline (links to VS-46/VS-11); treasury/banking (links to VS-18.2); finance (links to VS-17.4); encumbrance register (links to W3654); risk/ERM (links to VS-21.2); analytics (links to W3661)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/Sales forecast the surety demand from the B2G/B2B pipeline (links to VS-46/VS-11): bid bonds for upcoming tenders, performance bonds for expected awards, warranty bonds for deliveries, by value/term/provider; feed to capacity planning

Surety Program Manager/Treasury plan surety capacity and facility encumbrance: available facility (W3642), outstanding encumbrance (W3654), bank-credit encumbrance (links to VS-18.2), collateral/cash (W3644), and the headroom for new bids; flag capacity constraints and arrange additional facility if needed

Surety Program Manager/Risk assess the contingent-liability risk of the outstanding bond/guarantee portfolio (exposure to bond claim W3658), feed to ERM (links to VS-21.2) and treasury/cash planning (links to VS-18.1), and report capacity/encumbrance and risk to governance (W3661) and the risk committee (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, CFO, Treasury (links to VS-18), Legal (links to VS-100.3), B2G/B2B Sales (links to VS-46/VS-11), CEO, Board (links to VS-36), Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Program strategy (W3641); governance cycle; authority change

workflows.name: Surety Program Policy, Authority & Approval Matrix

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "report policy/authority effectiveness to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: issuance gate and audit; operational: annual review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Authority-bypass risk**: Bond committed without proper approval; mitigated by issuance gate and audit
- **Policy-staleness risk**: Outdated policy doesn't reflect current risk/market; mitigated by annual review
System Touchpoints: - Authority/capex (links to VS-40); governance/board (links to VS-36); legal (links to VS-100.3); audit (links to VS-21); encumbrance register (links to W3654)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/CFO maintain the surety policy: when a bond/guarantee is required (contract type/value/customer), the instrument-mix rules (W3641), the acceptable providers (W3643), the indemnity/collateral policy (W3644), and the contract-risk-assessment requirement before bonding

Surety Program Manager/CFO maintain the approval-authority matrix for bond/guarantee commitments by value/term/risk (Sales Manager → CFO → CEO → Board per links to VS-36), aligned to the capex/commitment authority (links to VS-40) and the board-delegated authorities; manage exceptions

Surety Program Manager/Audit enforce the policy and authority: gate bond issuance on approval (W3649–W3652), audit conformance, manage policy breaches, and report policy/authority effectiveness to governance (W3661) and audit (links to VS-21)

fields.Participants: Surety Program Manager, Audit (links to VS-21), Treasury (links to VS-18), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Finance (links to VS-17), Records (links to VS-88), Compliance (links to VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Annual audit cycle; regulatory inspection; claim/dispute

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Records maintain the surety documentation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Surety Program Manager/Audit conduct the annual surety-program audit" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "Surety Program Manager manage findings to closure, support regulatory" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: documentation discipline; operational: release tracking (W3657) and audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Records-gap risk**: Missing bond/indemnity records fail audit and weaken claim/defense position; mitigated by documentation discipline
- **Unreleased-bond risk**: Bonds completed but not released (capital/collateral trapped); mitigated by release tracking (W3657) and audit
System Touchpoints: - Records/retention (links to VS-88); audit (links to VS-21); finance/accounting (links to VS-17); compliance (links to VS-22); governance (links to VS-36); encumbrance register (links to W3654)

steps.activity: Surety Program Manager/Records maintain the surety documentation: facility agreements (W3642), GAI/counter-indemnity (W3644), provider contracts (W3643), each bond/guarantee instrument (W3650–W3652), the encumbrance register (W3654), releases (W3657), claims (W3658), and correspondence; retention per VS-88 and contract/regulation

Surety Program Manager/Audit conduct the annual surety-program audit: facility/capacity (W3642), encumbrance accuracy (W3654), collateral/indemnity (W3644), policy/authority conformance (W3647), released-bond completeness (W3657), and accounting/disclosure (links to VS-17); internal and (where required) external

Surety Program Manager manage findings to closure, support regulatory inspection (IC/BSP) and audit response (links to VS-22/W77), and report audit posture to the audit committee (links to VS-21/VS-36) and governance (W3661)
